newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Army said to back plan to oust Ecuador's Bucaram.
newsitem.headline: Army said to back plan to oust Ecuador's Bucaram.

text.p: Ecuador's lawmakers and powerful military leaders agreed on a plan on Sunday allowing Vice President Rosalia Arteaga to take over as interim president, a former presidential candidate said.

Juan Jose Castello, a leader of the left-leaning Popular Democratic Movement, told Reuters the plan was aimed at ending the constitutional crisis and growing sense of anarchy in Ecuador since Congress voted President Abdala Bucaram out of office last Thursday.

Castello said the plan was hammered out by legislators and senior military officials during a closed-door meeting at the Defense Ministry late on Saturday and had the full support of the armed forces.
An official announcement giving details of the plan, and specifying the period during which Arteaga would serve as president, was due to be made shortly, he added.

Bucaram, who was ousted in a congressional vote of no-confidence on Thursday, has dismissed the ruling as a de facto coup and said he remains the country's duly elected president. But both Arteaga and congressional leader Fabian Alarcon -- who Congress appointed to succeed Bucaram -- have laid legal claims to the presidency since Bucaram's ouster.
Under the agreement, Castello said Alarcon could be reappointed acting president by his fellow lawmakers as early as next Tuesday.
